facts.statement: The animal is classified under the genus Velociraptor.
facts.quote: taxon: Velociraptor

facts.statement: The genus Velociraptor was described by Henry Fairfield Osborn in 1924.
facts.quote: authority: Osborn, 1924

facts.statement: Velociraptor lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous epoch, approximately 75 to 71 million years ago.
facts.quote: lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous epoch, about 75 million to 71 million years ago (Mya)

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Velociraptor mongoliensis, which was named and described in 1924.
facts.quote: The type species is V. mongoliensis, named and described in 1924

facts.statement: Fossils of Velociraptor mongoliensis have been found in the Djadochta Formation in Mongolia.
facts.quote: Fossils of this species have been discovered in the Djadochta Formation, Mongolia

facts.statement: The species Velociraptor osmolskae was named in 2008 based on skull material from the Bayan Mandahu Formation in China.
facts.quote: A second species, V. osmolskae, was named in 2008 for skull material from the Bayan Mandahu Formation, China

facts.statement: In 1924, Henry Fairfield Osborn designated the skull and part of the hand as the type specimen for the new genus Velociraptor.
facts.quote: In 1924, museum president Henry Fairfield Osborn designated the skull and part of the manus as the type specimen of his new genus, Velociraptor

facts.statement: Osborn named the type species Velociraptor mongoliensis after Mongolia, the country where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: Osborn named the type species V. mongoliensis after its country of origin

facts.statement: The famous "Fighting Dinosaurs" specimen (MPC-D 100/25) was discovered by a Polish-Mongolian team in 1971.
facts.quote: The most famous is part of the "Fighting Dinosaurs" specimen (MPC-D 100/25; formerly IGM, GIN, or GI SPS), discovered by a Polish-Mongolian team in 1971

facts.statement: Specimen MPC-D 100/980 was nicknamed "Ichabodcraniosaurus" because it was a fairly complete skeleton found without its skull.
facts.quote: One such specimen, MPC-D 100/980, was nicknamed "Ichabodcraniosaurus" by Norell's team because the fairly complete specimen was found without its skull

facts.statement: In 1999, Rinchen Barsbold and Halszka Osmólska reported a juvenile Velociraptor specimen (GIN or IGM 100/2000) consisting of a complete skeleton with a skull.
facts.quote: In 1999, Rinchen Barsbold and Halszka Osmólska reported a juvenile Velociraptor specimen (GIN or IGM 100/2000), represented by a complete skeleton including the skull of a young individual

facts.statement: The juvenile specimen was found at the Tugriken Shireh locality in the Djadochta Formation during Mongolian-Japanese expeditions.
facts.quote: It was found at the Tugriken Shireh locality of the Djadochta Formation during the context of the Mongolian-Japanese Palaeontological Expeditions

facts.statement: Pascal Godefroit and colleagues named the bones V. osmolskae in 2008, honoring Polish paleontologist Halszka Osmólska.
facts.quote: Pascal Godefroit and colleagues named these bones V. osmolskae (for Polish paleontologist Halszka Osmólska) in 2008

facts.statement: In 1997, Mark A. Norell and Peter J. Makovicky described specimens MPC-D 100/985 and MPC-D 100/986 as V. mongoliensis, collected in 1993 from the Tugrik Shireh and Chimney Buttes localities respectively.
facts.quote: Paleontologists Mark A. Norell and Peter J. Makovicky in 1997 described new and well preserved specimens of V. mongoliensis, namely MPC-D 100/985 collected from the Tugrik Shireh locality in 1993, and MPC-D 100/986 collected in 1993 from the Chimney Buttes locality

facts.statement: Specimen MPC-D 100/982 was referred to V. mongoliensis based on skull similarities, though differences in the pelvic region were noted compared to other specimens.
facts.quote: MPC-D 100/982 was partially described and figured, and referred to V. mongoliensis mainly based on cranial similarities with the holotype skull, although they stated that differences were present between the pelvic region of this specimen and other Velociraptor specimens

facts.statement: In his 2020 master thesis, Mark J. Powers fully described MPC-D 100/982 and concluded it represents a new and third species of Velociraptor.
facts.quote: Mark J. Powers in his 2020 master thesis fully described MPC-D 100/982, which he concluded to represent a new and third species of Velociraptor

facts.statement: In 2021, Powers and colleagues used Principal Component Analysis to find that MPC-D 100/982 falls outside the variability of V. mongoliensis, arguing for its status as a distinct species.
facts.quote: In 2021 Powers with team used Principal Component Analysis to separate dromaeosaurid maxillae, most notably finding that MPC-D 100/982 falls outside the instraspecific variability of V. mongoliensis, arguing for a distinct species

facts.statement: Velociraptor was about 1.5 to 2.07 meters long with a body mass of approximately 14.1 to 19.7 kilograms.
facts.quote: Smaller than other dromaeosaurids like Deinonychus and Achillobator, Velociraptor was about 1.5 - 2.07 m long with a body mass of around 14.1 - 19.7 kg

facts.statement: Velociraptor is distinguished from other dromaeosaurids by its long, low skull with an upturned snout.
facts.quote: Velociraptor can be distinguished from other dromaeosaurids by its long and low skull, with an upturned snout

facts.statement: Adult Velociraptor measured between 1.5 and 2.07 meters long, about 0.5 meters high at the hips, and weighed approximately 14.1 to 19.7 kilograms.
facts.quote: Velociraptor was a small to medium-sized dromaeosaurid, with adults measuring between 1.5 - 2.07 m long, approximately 0.5 m high at the hips, and weighing about 14.1 - 19.7 kg

facts.statement: Some estimates suggest Velociraptor may have reached lengths of about 2.5 meters and weighed up to 28 kilograms.
facts.quote: Some estimates suggest that Velociraptor may have been larger, possibly reaching lengths of about 2.5 m (8 ft) and weighing up to 28 kg (60 lb)

facts.statement: Prominent quill knobs indicating feather attachment have been reported from the ulna of a Velociraptor specimen (IGM 100/981) estimated to be 1.5 meters long and 15 kilograms in weight.
facts.quote: Prominent quill knobs—attachment site of "wing" feathers and direct indicator of a feather covering—have been reported from the ulna of a single Velociraptor specimen (IGM 100/981), which represents an animal of estimated 1.5 m long and 15 kg in weight

facts.statement: A 2013 study suggested that V. osmolskae might not belong to the genus Velociraptor because phylogenetic analysis placed it closer to Linheraptor, making the genus paraphyletic, requiring reassessment.
facts.quote: However, the 2013 study noted that while "the elongate shape of the maxilla in V. osmolskae is similar to that of V. mongoliensis," phylogenetic analysis found it to be closer to Linheraptor, making the genus paraphyletic; thus, V. osmolskae might not actually belong to the genus Velociraptor and requires reassessment

facts.statement: The skull of Velociraptor was elongated and could reach a length of 23 cm.
facts.quote: The skull of Velociraptor was rather elongated and grew up to 23 cm long.

facts.statement: The snout made up about 60% of the skull length and was narrow, formed primarily by the nasal, premaxilla, and maxilla bones.
facts.quote: The snout, which occupied about 60% of the entire skull length, was notably narrow and mainly formed by the nasal, premaxilla, and maxilla bones.

facts.statement: The premaxilla was the frontmost bone of the skull and was longer than it was tall.
facts.quote: The premaxilla was the anteriormost bone in the skull, and it was longer than taller.

facts.statement: The maxilla was nearly triangular and was the largest bone element of the snout.
facts.quote: The maxilla was nearly triangular in shape and the largest element of the snout.

facts.statement: The premaxilla held 4 teeth sockets while the maxilla held 11.
facts.quote: The premaxilla had 4 alveoli (meaning that 4 teeth were developed), and the maxilla had 11 alveoli.

facts.statement: The dentary bone contained between 14 and 15 tooth sockets.
facts.quote: At the dentary, between 14–15 alveoli were present.

facts.statement: Maxillary teeth were slender and recurved, with the lower edge being more strongly serrated than the upper edge.
facts.quote: The maxillary teeth were more slender, recurved, and most notably, the lower end was strongly more serrated than the upper one.

facts.statement: Velociraptor had a large hand with three elongated fingers ending in strongly curved claws similar in construction to modern bird wing bones.
facts.quote: Velociraptor, like other dromaeosaurids, had a large manus with three elongated digits (fingers), which ended up in strongly curved unguals (claw bones) that were similar in construction and flexibility to the wing bones of modern birds.

facts.statement: The second finger was the longest of the three, while the first was the shortest.
facts.quote: The second digit was the longest of the three digits present, while the first was shortest.

facts.statement: Wrist bone structure prevented the wrist from turning inward, forcing the hand to be held with the palm facing inward rather than downward.
facts.quote: The structure of the carpal (wrist) bones prevented pronation of the wrist and forced the manus to be held with the palmar surface facing inward (medially), not downward.

facts.statement: The first toe was a small dewclaw, similar to other theropods.
facts.quote: The first digit, as in other theropods, was a small dewclaw.

facts.statement: The second toe was highly modified and held off the ground, causing Velociraptor to walk on its third and fourth toes.
facts.quote: The second digit, for which Velociraptor is most famous, was highly modified and held retracted off the ground, which caused Velociraptor and other dromaeosaurids to walk on only their third and fourth digits.

facts.statement: The second toe bore a large, sickle-shaped claw typical of dromaeosaurids and troodontids.
facts.quote: It bore a relatively large, sickle-shaped claw, typical of dromaeosaurid and troodontid dinosaurs.

facts.statement: The enlarged sickle claw could grow to over 6.5 cm in length and was likely used to restrain prey.
facts.quote: This enlarged claw, which could grow to over 6.5 cm long around its outer edge, was most likely a predatory device used to restrain struggling prey.

facts.statement: Prezygapophyses on the tail were once thought to stiffen the entire tail into a single rod-like unit.
facts.quote: These were once thought to fully stiffen the tail, forcing the entire tail to act as a single rod-like unit.

facts.statement: A specimen with tail vertebrae curved into an S-shape suggests the tail had more horizontal flexibility than previously thought.
facts.quote: However, at least one specimen has preserved a series of intact tail vertebrae curved sideways into an S-shape, suggesting that there was considerably more horizontal flexibility than once thought.

facts.statement: Velociraptor belongs to the group Eudromaeosauria, a subgroup of the family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: Velociraptor is a member of the group Eudromaeosauria, a derived sub-group of the larger family Dromaeosauridae.

facts.statement: Velociraptor is often classified within its own subfamily, Velociraptorinae.
facts.quote: It is often placed within its own subfamily, Velociraptorinae.

facts.statement: Some authors have classified all dromaeosaurids, including Velociraptor, in the family Archaeopterygidae, implying they are flightless birds.
facts.quote: All dromaeosaurids have also been referred to the family Archaeopterygidae by at least one author (which would, in effect, make Velociraptor a flightless bird).

facts.statement: Several studies suggest that V. osmolskae is distantly related to V. mongoliensis.
facts.quote: However, several studies have found "V." osmolskae to be distantly related to V. mongoliensis.

facts.statement: Studies from the 2010s suggest Velociraptorinae may not be a distinct group but rather a paraphyletic grade leading to Dromaeosaurinae.
facts.quote: Several studies published during the 2010s, including expanded versions of the analyses that found support for Velociraptorinae, have failed to resolve it as a distinct group, but rather have suggested it is a paraphyletic grade which gave rise to the Dromaeosaurinae.

facts.statement: In 2007, researchers found six quill knobs on the ulna of a Velociraptor specimen from the Djadochta Formation, indicating the presence of feathers.
facts.quote: In 2007 Alan H. Turner and colleagues reported the presence of six quill knobs in the ulna of a referred Velociraptor specimen (IGM 100/981) from the Ukhaa Tolgod locality of the Djadochta Formation.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that feathers on Velociraptor argue against the theory that large flightless maniraptorans lost feathers because of their size.
facts.quote: Turner and colleagues interpreted the presence of feathers on Velociraptor as evidence against the idea that the larger, flightless maniraptorans lost their feathers secondarily due to larger body size.

facts.statement: Velociraptor feathers may have served functions such as display, nest brooding, or aiding movement on slopes.
facts.quote: The feathers of the flightless Velociraptor may have been used for display, for covering their nests while brooding, or for added speed and thrust when running up inclined slopes.

facts.statement: It is debated whether a specific dromaeosaurid specimen from Ukhaa Tolgod should be classified as Velociraptor.
facts.quote: Napoli and team have noted that the referral of this specimen to Velociraptor is currently subject to reexamination.

facts.statement: Velociraptor could hear sound frequencies between 2,368 and 3,965 Hz, aiding in prey tracking.
facts.quote: Examinations of the endocranium of Velociraptor indicate that it was able to detect and hear a wide range of sound frequencies (2,368–3,965 Hz) and could track prey with ease as a result.

facts.statement: Velociraptor was an opportunistic predator that sometimes scavenged carrion, especially during droughts or if the animal was in poor health.
facts.quote: Fossil evidence suggesting Velociraptor scavenged also indicates that it was an opportunistic and actively predatory animal, feeding on carrion during times of drought or famine, if in poor health, or depending on the animal's age.

facts.statement: Velociraptor and relatives had elongated snouts adapted for picking up small, fast prey.
facts.quote: They found the maxilla to be a reliable reference when inferring the shape of the premaxilla and overall snout. For instance, most Asian species have elongated snouts based on the maxilla (namely velociraptorines), indicating a selective feeding in Velociraptor and relatives, such as picking up small, fast prey.

facts.statement: In 2022, a study estimated Velociraptor's bite force at 304 N, which is lower than that of Dromaeosaurus (885 N) and Deinonychus (706 N).
facts.quote: Manabu Sakamoto in 2022 performed a Bayesian phylogenetic predictive modelling framework for estimating jaw muscle parameters and bite forces of several extinct archosaurs, based on skull widths and phylogenetic relationships between groups. Among studied taxa, Velociraptor was scored with a bite force of 304 N, which was lower than that of other dromaeosaurids such as Dromaeosaurus (885 N) or Deinonychus (706 N).

facts.statement: A 1971 fossil specimen preserves a Velociraptor mongoliensis fighting a Protoceratops andrewsi, providing direct evidence of predatory behavior.
facts.quote: The "Fighting Dinosaurs" specimen, found in 1971, preserves a Velociraptor mongoliensis and Protoceratops andrewsi in combat and provides direct evidence of predatory behavior.

facts.statement: The "Fighting Dinosaurs" specimen is believed to have been buried rapidly by sand from a collapsing dune or sandstorm.
facts.quote: However, as the animals were preserved in ancient sand dune deposits, it is now thought that the animals were buried in sand, either from a collapsing dune or in a sandstorm.

facts.statement: Comparisons of scleral rings suggest Velociraptor may have been nocturnal, implying the "Fighting Dinosaurs" encounter occurred at twilight or in low light.
facts.quote: Comparisons between the scleral rings of Velociraptor, Protoceratops, and modern birds and reptiles indicates that Velociraptor may have been nocturnal, while Protoceratops may have been cathemeral, active throughout the day during short intervals, suggesting that the fight may have occurred at twilight or during low-light conditions.

facts.statement: The sickle claw on the second digit of dromaeosaurids was traditionally thought to be used for slashing and disemboweling prey.
facts.quote: The distinctive claw, on the second digit of dromaeosaurids, has traditionally been depicted as a slashing weapon; its assumed use being to cut and disembowel prey.

facts.statement: In the "Fighting Dinosaurs" fossil, the Velociraptor's sickle claw is embedded in the prey's throat while the prey's beak clamps the attacker's forelimb.
facts.quote: In the "Fighting Dinosaurs" specimen, the Velociraptor lies underneath, with one of its sickle claws apparently embedded in the throat of its prey, while the beak of Protoceratops is clamped down upon the right forelimb of its attacker.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Velociraptor used its sickle claw to pierce vital throat organs rather than slashing the abdomen.
facts.quote: This suggests Velociraptor may have used its sickle claw to pierce vital organs of the throat, such as the jugular vein, carotid artery, or trachea (windpipe), rather than slashing the abdomen.

facts.statement: The preserved bony core of the Velociraptor claw had a rounded inner edge, suggesting it was not suited for cutting or slashing.
facts.quote: The inside edge of the claw was rounded and not unusually sharp, which may have precluded any sort of cutting or slashing action, although only the bony core of the claw is preserved.

facts.statement: A 2005 BBC documentary test showed that a Velociraptor-like sickle claw could penetrate but not tear open a simulated abdominal wall, challenging the slashing hypothesis.
facts.quote: The slashing hypothesis was tested during a 2005 BBC documentary, The Truth About Killer Dinosaurs. The producers of the program created an artificial Velociraptor leg with a sickle claw and used a pork belly to simulate the dinosaur's prey. Though the sickle claw did penetrate the abdominal wall, it was unable to tear it open, indicating that the claw was not used to disembowel prey.

facts.statement: The only solid evidence for social behavior in dromaeosaurids is a Chinese trackway showing six individuals moving together.
facts.quote: However, the only solid evidence for social behavior of any kind among dromaeosaurids comes from a Chinese trackway which shows six individuals of a large species moving as a group.

facts.statement: Despite popular depictions, there is no specific fossil evidence that Velociraptor hunted in packs.
facts.quote: Therefore, while Velociraptor is commonly depicted as a pack hunter, as in Jurassic Park, there is only limited fossil evidence to support this theory for dromaeosaurids in general and none specific to Velociraptor itself.

facts.statement: In 2011, researchers proposed the "raptor prey restraint" model, suggesting dromaeosaurs pinned prey with their body weight and sickle claws before feeding.
facts.quote: In 2011, Denver Fowler and colleagues suggested a new method by which dromaeosaurs like Velociraptor and similar dromaeosaurs may have captured and restrained prey. This model, known as the "raptor prey restraint" (RPR) model of predation, proposes that dromaeosaurs killed their prey in a manner very similar to extant accipitrid birds of prey: by leaping onto their quarry, pinning it under their body weight, and gripping it tightly with the large, sickle-shaped claws.

facts.statement: The RPR model proposes that dromaeosaurs fed on living prey, causing death through blood loss and organ failure.
facts.quote: These researchers proposed that, like accipitrids, the dromaeosaur would then begin to feed on the animal while it was still alive, and prey death would eventually result from blood loss and organ failure.

facts.statement: Fowler found dromaeosaur feet and legs resemble eagles and hawks due to an enlarged second claw and grasping motion.
facts.quote: Fowler found that the feet and legs of dromaeosaurs most closely resemble those of eagles and hawks, especially in terms of having an enlarged second claw and a similar range of grasping motion.

facts.statement: Velociraptor arms, likely feathered, may have acted as stabilizers for balance while pinning prey, aided by a stiff tail.
facts.quote: The arms, which could exert a lot of force but were likely covered in long feathers, may have been used as flapping stabilizers for balance while atop a struggling prey animal, along with the stiff counterbalancing tail.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Velociraptor's weak jaws were used for sawing bites to finish off prey pinned by its limbs.
facts.quote: The jaws, thought by Fowler and colleagues to be comparatively weak, would have been useful for row saw motion bites like the modern day Komodo dragon, which also has a weak bite, to finish off its prey if the kicks were not powerful enough.

facts.statement: It is theorized that high bite force resistance in Velociraptor was an adaptation for scavenging rather than active predation.
facts.quote: It is theorized by the authors that high bite force resistance was an adaptation towards obtaining food through scavenging more often than through active predation in Velociraptor.

facts.statement: Velociraptor was warm-blooded to some degree due to its high energy requirements for hunting.
facts.quote: Velociraptor was warm-blooded to some degree, as it required a significant amount of energy to hunt.

facts.statement: Bone growth rates suggest Velociraptor had a more moderate metabolism compared to most modern warm-blooded mammals and birds.
facts.quote: However, bone growth rates in dromaeosaurids and some early birds suggest a more moderate metabolism, compared with most modern warm-blooded mammals and birds.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Velociraptor may not have possessed a fully developed nasal thermoregulation apparatus like modern endothermic animals.
facts.quote: Tada with team suggested that Velociraptor and most other non-avian dinosaurs may not have possessed a fully or well-developed nasal thermoregulation apparatus as modern endothermic animals do.

facts.statement: In 1995, researchers reported a Velociraptor skull with punctures matching the spacing and size of Velociraptor teeth.
facts.quote: Norell with colleagues in 1995 reported one V. mongoliensis skull bearing two parallel rows of small punctures on its frontal bones that, upon closer examination, match the spacing and size of Velociraptor teeth.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested that a wound on a Velociraptor skull was likely inflicted by another Velociraptor during an intraspecific fight.
facts.quote: They suggested that the wound was likely inflicted by another Velociraptor during a fight within the species.

facts.statement: In 2012, researchers reported an injured sub-adult Velociraptor specimen found with pterosaur bones in its stomach and a broken rib showing signs of healing.
facts.quote: In 2012 David Hone and team reported another injured Velociraptor specimen (MPC-D 100/54, roughly a sub-adult individual) found with the bones of an azhdarchid pterosaur within its stomach cavity, was carrying or recovering from an injury sustained to one broken rib.

facts.statement: Velociraptor lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: Velociraptor lived between 75 and 71 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Velociraptor (lat. 'ladrón veloz') es un género con dos especies conocidas de dinosaurios terópodos dromeosáuridos que vivieron hacia finales del período Cretácico, hace de 75 a 71 millones de años, durante el Campaniaense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Velociraptor was a bipedal carnivore with a long rigid tail, characteristic feathers, and a large sickle-shaped claw on each foot likely used for killing prey.
facts.quote: Fue un carnívoro bípedo, con una cola larga y rígida, con plumas características y una uña grande con forma de hoz en cada pata, que probablemente le facilitaba el matar a sus presas.

facts.statement: Unlike other dromaeosaurids, Velociraptor had a low elongated skull and a flat snout directed upward.
facts.quote: A diferencia de otros dromeosáuridos, Velociraptor poseía un cráneo bajo y alargado, y un hocico chato, dirigido hacia arriba.

facts.statement: Velociraptor was approximately the size of a turkey, much smaller than the two-meter, ninety-kilogram dinosaurs depicted in novels and films, and more similar in size to Deinonychus.
facts.quote: El Velociraptor era aproximadamente del tamaño de un pavo, considerablemente más pequeño que los dinosaurios de dos metros de altura y noventa kilogramos que aparecen en novelas y películas, más similares a Deinonychus.

facts.statement: Velociraptor size ranged from 1.5 to 2.07 meters in length with a body mass between 15 and 18.3 kilograms.
facts.quote: El rango de tamaños varía de 1.5 a 2.07 m de largo, con una masa corporal de entre 15 y 18.3 kg.

facts.statement: Velociraptor may have been covered in feathers, including complex feathers on its forearms similar to modern bird wing feathers.
facts.quote: Es posible que Velociraptor estuviese cubierto de plumas, no solo plumón cobertor sino que también presentara plumas complejas en los antebrazos semejantes a las rémiges de las aves actuales.

facts.statement: The genus Velociraptor was named by Osborn in 1924.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Osborn, 1924

facts.statement: The type species of Velociraptor is Velociraptor mongoliensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Velociraptor mongoliensis

facts.statement: Velociraptor osmolskae was described by Godefroit et al. in 2008.
facts.quote: subdivision: Velociraptor osmolskae Godefroit et al., 2008

facts.statement: Velociraptor is a genus of two known species of dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Velociraptor (lat. 'ladrón veloz') es un género con dos especies conocidas de dinosaurios terópodos dromeosáuridos

facts.statement: A second species, Velociraptor osmolskae, was named in 2008 based on cranial material from Inner Mongolia, China.
facts.quote: una segunda especie, Velociraptor osmolskae, fue nombrada en 2008 a partir de material craneal procedente de Mongolia Interior, en China.

facts.statement: A particularly famous specimen shows a Velociraptor engaged in a battle with a Protoceratops.
facts.quote: Un espécimen particularmente famoso es el que muestra a un Velociraptor enzarzado en una batalla con un Protoceratops.

facts.statement: The snout occupied about 60% of the total skull length and was notably narrow, formed mainly by the nasal, premaxilla, and maxilla bones.
facts.quote: El hocico, que ocupaba alrededor del 60 % de la longitud total del cráneo, era notablemente estrecho y estaba formado principalmente por los huesos nasal, premaxilar y maxilar.

facts.statement: The premaxilla was the most anterior bone of the skull and was longer than it was tall.
facts.quote: El premaxilar era el hueso más anterior del cráneo y era más largo que alto.

facts.statement: The maxilla was nearly triangular in shape and was the largest element of the snout.
facts.quote: El maxilar tenía forma casi triangular y era el elemento más grande del hocico.

facts.statement: The lacrimal bone was T-shaped with a main body that was thin and delicate.
facts.quote: El lagrimal era un hueso en forma de T y su cuerpo principal era delgado y delicado.

facts.statement: The eye socket, formed by the lacrimal, jugal, frontal, and postorbital bones, was large, nearly circular, and longer than it was tall.
facts.quote: La órbita o fenestra orbital, la cavidad del ojo, formada por el lagrimal, el yugal, el frontal y el postorbitario, era grande y de forma casi circular, siendo más larga que alta.

facts.statement: The most posterior bone was the occipital, projecting into a rounded, bulbous occipital condyle that met the first neck vertebra.
facts.quote: El hueso más posterior era el hueso occipital y su proyección el cóndilo occipital, una protuberancia redondeada y bulbosa que se encuentra con la primera vértebra del cuello.

facts.statement: The dentary was a very long, weakly curved, and narrow bone that developed several alveoli on its upper surface.
facts.quote: El dentario era un elemento muy largo, débilmente curvado y estrecho que desarrollaba varios alvéolos en su superficie superior.

facts.statement: The premaxilla had four alveoli for four teeth, while the maxilla had eleven alveoli.
facts.quote: El premaxilar tenía cuatro alvéolos, lo que significa que se desarrollaron cuatro dientes, y el maxilar tenía once alvéolos.

facts.statement: Between fourteen and fifteen alveoli were present in the dentary.
facts.quote: En el dentario, estaban presentes entre catorce y quince alvéolos.

facts.statement: Velociraptor teeth were fairly homodont (similar in shape) and had denticles that were serrated more on the rear edge than the front.
facts.quote: Los dientes de Velociraptor eran bastante homodontos, iguales en forma, y tenían varios dentículos, cada uno más aserrado en el borde posterior que en el frontal.

facts.statement: Maxillary teeth were thinner and recurved, with the lower edge significantly more serrated than the upper, possibly an adaptation to capture and hold fast prey.
facts.quote: Los dientes maxilares eran más delgados, recurvados y, sobre todo, el extremo inferior estaba considerablemente más aserrado que el superior, posiblemente una adaptación que mejoró su habilidad para capturar y retener presas veloces.

facts.statement: Like other dromaeosaurids, Velociraptor had a large hand with three elongated fingers ending in strongly curved claw bones similar in construction and flexibility to modern bird wing bones.
facts.quote: Velociraptor, al igual que otros dromeosáuridos, tenía una mano grande con tres dedos alargados que terminaban en unguales fuertemente curvados, huesos de garras, que eran similares en construcción y flexibilidad a los huesos de las alas de las aves modernas.

facts.statement: The second digit was the longest of the three, while the first was the shortest.
facts.quote: El segundo dígito fue el más largo de los tres dígitos presentes, mientras que el primero fue el más corto.

facts.statement: The carpal bone structure prevented wrist pronation and forced the palm surface to face inward medially rather than downward.
